text: dsh-plugin-bridge 是面向 DSH Web 与 Desktop 的会话迁移插件：它注册 /bridge 命令，并可提供自然语言预览工具。插件读取源会话内容，生成有固定结构的交接摘要，供用户预览和编辑后再确认创建目标会话；支持选择目标 preset、调整摘要文本，并在新会话中继续交接流程。原会话保持不变。适合需要把当前任务切换到另一种 preset 或模式的 DSH 用户。摘要由宿主模型生成，使用前需在兼容的 DSH 主机安装插件并配置模型。

dsh-plugin-bridge adds /bridge for DSH session handoffs across presets. It creates an editable summary from the source session; users review and confirm before a target session is created. The source stays unchanged. An optional tool prepares previews using the host model.
想把当前 DSH 会话的任务交接到另一个 preset。
能不能先生成可编辑的会话迁移摘要，确认后再开新会话？
我需要把当前对话整理成结构化交接内容。
切换到另一种工作模式时，怎样保留会话里的任务状态？
让 DSH 创建新会话前先给我检查和修改交接摘要。
我想把一个会话的后续步骤带到新的 preset 中继续。
How can I review and edit a session handoff before moving to another preset?
I want to carry the current task context into a new DSH session.
Can DSH prepare a structured summary for switching work modes?
Move this conversation to a different preset while keeping its task state.
dsh-plugin-bridge 的功能「预览交接摘要」：/bridge 命令读取源会话并生成固定结构的摘要，供确认前检查。
dsh-plugin-bridge 的功能「编辑摘要」：用户可在原生 Bridge 卡片中查看和编辑摘要，再选择是否确认迁移。
dsh-plugin-bridge 的功能「选择目标 preset」：迁移流程列出可用 preset，并解析 code 与 ptc 的兼容名称。
dsh-plugin-bridge 的功能「继续交接任务」：确认后创建目标会话并注入交接内容，可配置目标会话的注入方式。
dsh-plugin-bridge 的功能「自然语言准备」：可选的 bridge_prepare 工具只准备用户审核用的预览，不直接执行迁移。
dsh-plugin-bridge 使用前须知：摘要预览由宿主模型生成，实际模型由源会话和插件配置决定（见 src/migrate.ts:95-125）。
dsh-plugin-bridge 使用前须知：bridge_prepare 仅准备供用户审核的预览，用户仍需在界面中确认迁移（见 src/natural-language.ts:80-110）。

dsh-plugin-bridge README · dsh-plugin-bridge：Halfway through a task and need another tool preset? Switching the produced session in place would leave tool history that belongs to the old assembly. Bridge previews a bounded five-part handoff, opens a clean target, and leaves the original session untouched.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · dsh-plugin-bridge：[Quick start](#quick-start) · [Why Bridge](#why-bridge) · [Evidence](#evidence-at-a-glance) · [Decisions](#migration-decisions) · [Compatibility](#compatibility)

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Quick start：Bridge **0.5.2** admits the published DSH **0.2.2** line through stable 0.2.2, including `0.2.2-rc.1`. Bridge **0.5.1** admitted the 0.2.2 alpha line, including published `0.2.2-alpha.2`. Bridge **0.5.0** adds a conversation-menu action, a configurable shortcut and natural-language preparation, while keeping preview, editing and human confirmation. The 0.5.0 candidate passed isolated official **0.2.1-rc.2 Web and native macOS Desktop** handoffs and a keyless **0.2.0-rc.2** backward check. The [acceptance record](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.2.1-rc.2-entrypoints-2026-10-18.md) separates runtime tests, their limits and pending publication checks. Admission of a later alpha is not that acceptance; see [Support policy](#support-policy).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Quick start：Check the Host's **actual pnpm executable** when installing or removing packages. pnpm 11.22.0 has a known late-worker shutdown bug that can keep a package operation alive after printing Done; natural DSH reproductions isolated the upstream fixes. Use **11.26.0 or later**, which includes the [upstream fixes](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v11.26.0), and avoid **overlapping package operations**. If an operation is pending, wait for it to settle or stop the Host normally before using the offline CLI. Bridge does not bundle pnpm or upgrade your tools automatically.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · npm / CLI：Install from npm:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-bridge
```

On **DSH 0.1.5-rc.2**, restart `dsh web` after adding or removing the plugin. On **DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2**, a first install from the WebUI Plugins page applies live; CLI install and upgrades may still need one restart. **DSH 0.1.7-alpha.1** was tested with CLI installation, live disable/enable, and removal followed by a restart; restart-free installation or upgrades were not tested.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · npm / CLI：On **DSH 0.2.1-alpha.3 / 0.2.1-alpha.4 Web** with HMR, the running `pluginManager` service's `installBundle()` API, including Remote API callers and the agent's `plugin_manager` tool, returns `already-installed` for a package already in the profile, even when another version is requested. API replacement uses `removeBundle(name)` followed by `installBundle(spec)`; honor any restart request. See the [upstream upgrade guide](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.4/docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-alpha.2/plugin-install-over-installed/guide.md).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · npm / CLI：For CLI replacement, stop the Host using the selected profile, run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-bridge`, then `dsh plugin --profile web add <desired-package-spec>`, and start the Host again. The [CLI runs separate profile package operations](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.3/apps/cli/src/plugin.ts); the running-API refusal above does not apply to that path.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · npm / CLI：Before either replacement, finish or save pending handoffs: previews and unconfirmed edits live in memory and stopping or unloading Bridge discards their confirmation state. The source session remains intact; generate a new preview after reinstallation and reapply any saved draft. These Web procedures do not upgrade Desktop; native Desktop acceptance is [recorded separately for **0.2.1-rc.2**](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.2.1-rc.2-entrypoints-2026-10-18.md#native-macos-desktop-acceptance).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · npm / CLI：Pinned GitHub fallback:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Totoro-qaq/dsh-plugin-bridge#v0.5.2
```

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Discover：On DSH versions with Discover (introduced in **0.2.1-alpha.4**), you can also install Bridge from the author's index:

1. Open **Plugins → Experimental plugins → More** and enable **Custom plugin markets**.
2. Open **Discover → Add index source** and paste:

```text

   ```
dsh-plugin-bridge README · Discover：3. Choose **Bridge**, check the package name, version and `https://registry.npmjs.org/` in the confirmation, then install and choose **Enable now**.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Discover：This is an [author-hosted third-party source](https://github.com/Totoro-qaq/dsh-plugin-index), not official certification or community approval. It must be added to each profile you want to use it in. Adding and installing from the public URL was [verified on an isolated alpha.4 WebUI](https://github.com/Totoro-qaq/dsh-plugin-index/blob/main/docs/acceptance-2026-10-16.md); clients without Discover can keep using npm/CLI above. The Discover installation path was not separately re-tested on native Desktop.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Three entrypoints：- **Menu action:** open the current conversation's `⋯` menu in the sidebar and choose **Hand off session**. This opens the target picker without replacing a draft or submitting attachments. The composer's existing Bridge item also works when offered; DSH hides argument-taking commands from its `+` menu when the draft is nonempty. No permanent header button or extra command is added.
- **Keyboard:** search for **Bridge** in DSH keyboard settings and bind **Hand off current session**. The command is unbound by default and takes no system, Host, or other plugin shortcut; its ID is `dsh-plugin-bridge.open`.
- **Natural language:** say, for example, “Hand this task off to PTC; let me review the summary first.” Modes with model-tool support can call `bridge_prepare`. An omitted target opens the picker. The model can prepare a handoff, not confirm it for you.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Three entrypoints：All paths keep **human confirmation**: choose a target → preview → edit Text/Markdown → confirm. Existing `/bridge` commands remain available. Hosts without the optional UI/tool services retain the command fallback. The shortcut acts only on the current conversation, not a separate main panel such as Jot or an open modal.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Three entrypoints：Natural language is on by default. Set `naturalLanguage: false` in Bridge configuration to disable it without disabling the button, keyboard command, or slash command. Enabling it adds tool-description tokens; ordinary requests are no longer universally zero-overhead. See [entrypoint and confirmation boundaries](docs/entrypoints.md).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Existing commands：Then type in the official WebUI:

```text
/bridge                       list target presets
/bridge --doctor              check the host contract after a DSH upgrade
/bridge code                  preview the handoff; change nothing
/bridge code --go             migrate, restate, then wait

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Existing commands：On DSH rc.7 and later, the official WebUI renders `/bridge` as a native card. **Text** exposes the fixed five sections as ordinary fields and flat bullet or ordered-list rows while preserving their Markdown markers; **Markdown** preserves full source freedom; **Preview** renders Markdown or a complete JSON tree. Long content scrolls inside the card. **Confirm migration** opens the created target session. Bridge 0.3.10 adds room to keep confirmation reachable above the fixed composer at the tested narrow widths.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Existing commands：UIs that implement the official `conversation.chat.commandview` slot receive the same card automatically. Other custom UIs retain the complete server result, summary-file workflow, and target title/session-ID fallback; UI authors can reuse the framework-free `dsh-plugin-bridge/client-contract` export instead of reimplementing the wire. On an older or non-slot client, correct the printed summary file and run:

```text
/bridge code --go --file <path>
```

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Existing commands：Preview edits are temporary until migration is confirmed. Restarting the client or system may discard them; the source session remains untouched, and you can regenerate the preview.

Uninstall with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-plugin-bridge`, then restart `dsh web`.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Why Bridge：| Promise | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Preview before execution** | `/bridge <preset>` creates no target and changes no source session. Review or edit the five-section handoff first. |
| **Move state, not tool traces** | Decisions, paths, current state, and next steps move to a clean preset. Incompatible calls from the old tool assembly do not. |
| **Fail closed** | The target goal is paused before kickoff. If that cannot be guaranteed, Bridge clears/cancels the target and sends no model request. |

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Why Bridge：With natural language disabled (`naturalLanguage: false`), the button, keyboard command, and `/bridge` are dispatched by the Host without a Bridge model-tool description. The default natural-language entry registers one preview-only tool; a summary worker runs only when a handoff is requested.
dsh-plugin-bridge README · Evidence at a glance：The release gate is intentionally small and reproducible; these are regression results, not population guarantees.

|---|---:|
| Five-part summary facts | **30/30** |
| Target restatement / first useful work facts | **60/60 · 60/60** |
| Critical facts / obsolete-value resurrection | **90/90 · 0** |
| Existing image evidence / unresolved raw image | **5/5 · 5/5** |

| Native WebUI repeat gate (preview / target facts) | **3/3 · 3/3**, five facts each |

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Evidence at a glance：The token percentage varies widely with preset, response length, and cache state. The worker share is composition, not causal overhead versus no Bridge; the stable product claim is one additional confirmation request. Read the [design and evidence boundaries](docs/design.md), [full release report](reports/v0.2.3-e2e-report.md), and [vision report](reports/v0.2.6-rc11-vision-report.md).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · How it works：```text
fold history -> five-part handoff -> preview/edit -> clean target session
             -> pause stored goal -> inject -> restate -> wait or continue
image history -> verbatim assistant evidence; unresolved originals use the attachment gateway
```

The five sections are Goal, Current state, Key decisions and conventions, Key files, and Next step. The original session is never rewritten; archive the target and return to the source if the handoff is unsatisfactory.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Migration decisions：| Situation | Bridge behavior | Cost / fidelity effect |
|---|---|---|
| `naturalLanguage: false`, no handoff requested | No prompt injection or model tool | **0 Bridge prompt tokens** |
| Natural language enabled, no handoff requested | `bridge_prepare` tool description registered | Tool-description overhead; no summary-worker request |
| `/bridge code` | One bounded summary worker; preview only | No target session is created |
| Default `--go` | Target restates and waits | One explicit confirmation request before useful work |
| `--go --continue` | Confirm the defined next step; restate and work in one target request | Separate approvals and safety limits still apply; no background goal round |
| Image already has assistant analysis | Copy that response verbatim | No raw image is resent by default |
| Image is unresolved and target accepts images | Copy the original attachment and preserve the source VLM | Vision pricing comes from the selected provider |
| Image is unresolved and target is text-only | Prompt admission rejects the image; Bridge sends a visible text fallback | No hidden local VLM and no silent claim of visual understa

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：From Bridge **0.4.7**, `engines.dsh` is an installation-admission range, not an exact list of tested releases. Bridge **0.5.2** keeps that policy and widens the 0.2.2 clause so published `0.2.2-rc.1` matches. Bridge **0.5.1** admitted the alpha line after comparing `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-alpha.2` with the already admitted `0.2.1-rc.4`:

```text
>=0.1.0-rc.7 <0.2.0-0 || 0.2.0-rc.2 || >=0.2.1-alpha.1 <0.2.2-0 || >=0.2.2-alpha <0.2.3-0
```

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：The previous host terms are unchanged. The 0.2.1 term still admits later alpha/beta/rc builds and final 0.2.1, and its `<0.2.2-0` ceiling still excludes every 0.2.2 prerelease. The separate `>=0.2.2-alpha <0.2.3-0` term admits `0.2.2-alpha` and later `0.2.2-alpha.*`, including published `0.2.2-alpha.2` and `0.2.2-alpha.3`, then beta, rc (including published `0.2.2-rc.1`) and stable 0.2.2. The ceiling is `0.2.3-0`, so every 0.2.3 prerelease stays outside. The previous ceiling `<0.2.2-beta` rejected `0.2.2-rc.1` because `rc` sorts after `beta`. `0.2.2-0` stays below the `0.2.2-alpha` lower bound. DSH evaluates this field with `includePrerelease: true`. A caret such as `^0.2.1-alpha.1` (`>=0.2.1-alpha.1 <0.3.0-0`) would also admit later 0.2.x prereleases, including 0.2.3; this range stops at the next patch prerelease.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：`0.2.2-alpha.2` removed `sessionController.inspect`. Bridge reads that host's history through `sessionController.events` (or the deprecated `page` alias) and still uses `sessionController.inspect` when the host provides it. Command registration, goals, plan-review actions, shortcuts and the client slots Bridge uses stayed compatible. This adapter change is not a Web or Desktop acceptance of `0.2.2-alpha.2`. That host requires Node.js `>=24.9.0`; Bridge's own Node declaration stays `>=22` for older hosts. The development SDK pins remain `0.2.1-alpha.4`.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Admission is not acceptance. The table, version-specific reports and Workshop's exact `dshVersions` name only exercised hosts. Published package metadata is a snapshot; later passing documentation checks do not silently rewrite an old npm artifact. Compatible updates inside an admitted line need a diff review and short acceptance pass, not a new npm release merely to append an alpha number. Actual code/dependency/packaging fixes still require a release, and a new version family requires reviewing the boundary. The verified exact alpha.4 development SDK baseline is retained; it does not have to advance for every compatible Host. `/bridge --doctor` helps identify missing capabilities but does not replace migration acceptance.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Since Bridge **0.4.0**, **Approve in new session** is available on the official plan-review card, verified on DSH **0.2.0-rc.2** and **0.2.1-alpha.1** WebUI. Enter `/plan` and review the plan submitted through `exit_plan_mode`, then choose the Bridge action. It stops the original planning turn, leaves that session in plan mode, creates a fresh session with the same preset/model/workspace, transfers the approved plan verbatim in its kickoff, and starts implementation there. The host's existing **Approve** and **Request changes** controls keep their ordinary behavior. See [the approved-plan workflow](docs/approved-plan-handoff.md).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Published Bridge **0.4.1** also passed [native macOS Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2 acceptance](docs/compatibility/desktop-0.2.0-rc.2-2026-10-05.md): installation, edited migration, approved-plan execution, live toggles, uninstall and restart. Desktop and npm WebUI records are separate; native-window pixels and account login are not certified.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：The **0.5.0 candidate** additionally passed [native macOS Desktop 0.2.1-rc.2 acceptance](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.2.1-rc.2-entrypoints-2026-10-18.md#native-macos-desktop-acceptance): GUI installation, shortcut binding/remapping, the conversation menu, a real natural-language preview, exact edited handoff, automatic target opening, normal quit, restart and GUI removal. This does not re-certify approved-plan execution, native IME/paste integration, account login or every third-party UI/plugin combination.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：| DSH baseline | Server handoff | Native card | Verification boundary |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 0.2.1-rc.2 | Yes (Bridge 0.5.0 candidate) | Web and native macOS Desktop passed | Official isolated Web and Desktop, doctor 13/13; menu, configurable shortcut and real natural-language preview; Text/Markdown editing and explicit PTC confirmation with a paused one-round goal. Web also passed inflight disposal, neighboring-plugin coexistence and removal/restart; Desktop passed normal quit, restart and GUI removal. Exact 1,519-character native handoff and remaining limits are in the [candidate record](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.2.1-rc.2-entrypoints-2026-10-18.md). Local candidate acceptance is not npm publication or a claim that every optional feature was re-tested. |
| 0.2.1-alpha.5 | Yes (Bridge 0.4.7) | Real edit/confirm/auto-open passed | Official npm Host; no exemption, doctor 13/13, one preview worker, exact 1,856-character UI-reviewed payload into PTC with a paused goal, one target turn and zero target tools. Text/Markdown round-trip, bounded editor scrolling, current-directory placement, toggles, restart, removal and absence of the CLI shim pass

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Bridge 0.4.2 adds exact `0.2.1-alpha.2` to `engines.dsh` and fixes two runtime issues: stale working-directory placement and false worker-start detection after a history window trims `turn/start`. Published 0.4.1 does not contain these fixes. rc.2 Desktop and alpha.1 backward smoke checks are recorded separately from alpha.2 Web acceptance.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Historical declaration: Bridge **0.4.6** added only exact `0.2.1-alpha.4` to the existing host range and built against that SDK with Cordis `4.0.5-alpha.2`. Bridge 0.4.5's narrower engine excluded alpha.4 under the Host's installer rules; no compatibility exemption was used. Business source and generated `lib/` were unchanged, and keyless backward startup/doctor/client-resource/removal checks passed on official 0.2.0-rc.2 and alpha.3 Web Hosts. The alpha.4 core workflow and fixed-package-manager removal controls passed; the earlier failed operation remains recorded. Local checks, bounded Host results and release/tag/npm publication are separate gates. Later prereleases and stable 0.2 releases were outside that 0.4.6 declaration; the bounded policy above supersedes it from 0.4.7. Hot replacement with different-business-byte packages was not tested, so Workshop activation remains `restart-host` and hot-reload evidence remains unset. Approved-plan real execution, images, native alpha.4 Desktop, Windows and Linux were not re-certified.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Use Bridge 0.3.4 or later for DSH 0.1.5-alpha.1: DSH published no 0.1.4, and a caret prerelease range such as `^0.1.3-alpha.2` never matches the next prerelease minor, so 0.3.4 adds `^0.1.5-alpha.1` and builds against that SDK with byte-identical `lib/` output. Session format V3 records the system prompt as a `system/message` surface node; Bridge folds only user, assistant and tool events, so prompt text never enters a handoff. Use Bridge 0.3.3 or later for DSH 0.1.3-alpha.2; Bridge 0.3.2 does not include those compatibility changes. The typed adapter reads the default 240-message history window with one fresh `inspect` call instead of four; it does not cache running state. `doctor` checks method availability, not end-to-end compatibility. The same `^0.1.5-alpha.1` range also matches 0.1.5-rc.1 and the 0.1.5 final, so rc.1 needs no new Bridge release.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Since 0.3.5 the summary worker follows the conversation's model by default (`modelTier: current`). On DSH 0.1.5-rc.1 that is V4.1-Flash, which matched V4-Pro in the [tier comparison](reports/worker-tier-rc1-2026-09-10.md) at about half the summary time. DSH releases before 0.1.5-rc.1 have no V4.1-Flash, so set `DSH_BRIDGE_TIER=pro` or pass `--tier pro` there.

Use Bridge 0.3.6 or later for DSH 0.1.6-alpha.1 (only the dependency ranges changed; shipped code was the same as 0.3.5).

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Since 0.3.8 the five DSH optional peer ranges are `"*"`; `engines.dsh` expresses the host support declaration. Bridge 0.4.1 declares `>=0.1.0-rc.7 <0.2.0-0 || 0.2.0-rc.2 || 0.2.1-alpha.1`: it preserves the previous range and adds only the newly tested alpha.1, not later 0.2 prereleases or stable 0.2.0/0.2.1. dshmarket evaluates this field with `includePrerelease: true`; the official 0.2.0-rc.2 installer instead checks DSH peer ranges, so installation alone does not establish verified support.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2 removed the client `sessions.open`. Bridge 0.3.6 still migrates there, but its **Open target session** button fails with `ctx.sessions.open is not a function`. Use Bridge 0.3.7 or later: it opens targets through the WebUI navigation service `uiWorkspace.openSession` and falls back to `sessions.open` on older hosts.

CI covers Node.js 22 and 24. Run `/bridge --doctor` after every Harness upgrade; it names missing required gateway methods instead of failing vaguely.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：DSH 0.1.7-alpha.1 was verified on macOS with Node 22.23.1 and the published Bridge 0.3.9, without a runtime or dependency change. The V3→V4 test used a copy of an existing test home; back up `DSH_HOME`, including sessions and profiles, before upgrading. Custom directory-based preset migration, other UI/plugin combinations, and Windows were not covered. This acceptance does not require another Bridge npm release.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：Bridge 0.3.10 includes the source build tested on DSH 0.1.7-alpha.2. It fixes two observed edges: an omitting summary worker no longer silently drops narrowly recognized, still-active user prohibitions on using tools or reading/writing files from the editable handoff, and the confirmation control remains clickable in the tested small viewports. Later explicit permission supersedes an earlier prohibition. This is a guard for these explicit forms, **not** a guarantee that every user constraint is automatically retained; review and edit the handoff before confirming. The confirmed draft is still sent exactly as edited. The linked acceptance predates npm publication and should not be read as registry-install evidence.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：The published Bridge 0.3.10 also passed a bounded DSH 0.1.7-rc.1 compatibility run. No Bridge runtime change or new npm release was needed. This does **not** validate every optional DSH dependency or third-party UI; follow the [rc.1 test boundary](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.1.7-rc.1-2026-09-24.md) and run `/bridge --doctor` after upgrading your own host.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：For DSH **0.2.0-rc.2**, Bridge **0.3.11** updates the support metadata and documentation; the migration runtime remains unchanged from the tested published 0.3.10. The [acceptance record](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.2.0-rc.2-2026-09-30.md) separates real-model/WebUI evidence from packaging checks. It does not certify stable DSH 0.2.0, native Desktop login/quit, all optional components, or third-party UIs.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Support policy：For DSH **0.2.1-alpha.1**, Bridge **0.4.1** updates support metadata and documentation; server/client code, generated `lib/`, SDK pins and dependencies remain unchanged from 0.4.0. The [acceptance record](docs/compatibility/dsh-0.2.1-alpha.1-2026-10-04.md) documents real-model flows and lifecycle checks. Images, native Desktop, later alpha versions and arbitrary plugin/UI combinations were not re-certified in this run.

dsh-plugin-bridge README · Development：```bash
npm ci
npm run verify
```

`verify` builds and type-checks both plugin halves, runs the regression suite, checks generated `lib/` and datasets, then packs, installs, and imports the actual npm tarball. The SDK guards check installed manifests as well as package and lockfile declarations. Tests spend no model tokens. `prepublishOnly` runs the same gate; GitHub releases also require the tag to match `package.json` before trusted npm publishing.
